result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers use the finding as the headline, and their arithmetic checks out (8,750→9,530 is +9%, 10,440 is +19%, 164→231 is +41%, 155 plots, +18% volunteer hours). B leads with the like-for-like 9% for the four established gardens and gives the all-gardens 19% only as context. A opens with the inflated 19% and builds its 'more than double' comparison bar on it, and its waitlist axis says Nov 15 when the data gives only Nov 2026. B's zero-based waitlist columns with direct labels and its clean layout of KPI cards plus two charts read more cohesively. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers use the finding as the headline, and their arithmetic checks out (8,750→9,530 kg is +9%, 164→231 people is +41%). A leads with the like-for-like +9% for the four gardens open in both years, states the Nov 15 cut-off throughout, and labels its zero-based bars directly, all in a clean two-visual layout. B's opening subtitle claims 19% growth by counting the new Pepper Hill site, which overstates growth even though it is clarified later. B also uses a waitlist line chart with gridlines, rounds 6.7 people a month down to 'roughly 6', and spreads across three busier columns.
